title: Fallback Prompt Strategies
summary: Use evaluated alternate prompt strategies for specific recoverable failure classes while preserving policy, evidence requirements, and response contracts.
overview: Fallback prompt strategies change how a task is presented when the primary prompt fails in a recognizable way. Examples include a simpler extraction prompt after formatting failure, a narrower evidence question after an overbroad answer, or a clarification request when required input is absent. Fallback is a controlled branch with its own evaluation, not an improvised attempt to bypass a refusal.

Keep mandatory constraints invariant across prompts. Authorization, sensitive-data rules, required citations, and factual uncertainty cannot disappear because a shorter prompt seems more likely to succeed. Classify the failure first: service outages call for operational recovery, while missing evidence calls for retrieval or abstention rather than different wording.

production.poc: A prototype can compare one alternate prompt against the primary on a known defect set. Include normal cases to detect regressions introduced by the fallback.
production.production: Production maintains a versioned prompt registry, explicit trigger conditions, bounded attempts, and shared output validation. Record which strategy actually produced the accepted result.
production.scale: At scale, monitor fallback frequency and total cost. A fallback that handles most traffic may indicate that it should become the primary, while a low-success branch should be removed rather than retained as ritual complexity.

components.name: Failure classifier
components.role: Identifies formatting, ambiguity, coverage, or other explicitly recoverable prompt-level defects.

components.name: Prompt registry
components.role: Stores approved primary and fallback templates with versions and invariant constraints.

components.name: Strategy selector
components.role: Chooses a tested alternative for the observed failure class.

components.name: Shared validator
components.role: Applies the same required schema, evidence, and policy checks to every strategy.

components.name: Outcome recorder
components.role: Measures branch usage, recovery success, added cost, and introduced regressions.

flow.title: Run primary strategy
flow.description: Execute the normal prompt with the task's evidence and required constraints.

flow.title: Inspect failure
flow.description: Determine whether the defect can plausibly be repaired through a different prompting approach.

flow.title: Select approved fallback
flow.description: Choose the mapped strategy without weakening policy or inventing missing data.

flow.title: Reassemble context
flow.description: Preserve essential evidence and constraints while simplifying irrelevant instructions.

flow.title: Validate alternative
flow.description: Apply the same acceptance tests used for the primary result.

flow.title: Stop or promote result
flow.description: Accept the supported output or terminate after the bounded strategy budget is exhausted.

diagrams.caption: The fallback changes task presentation while acceptance and policy remain constant.

useCase.title: Extracting fields from an unusual bill of lading
useCase.situation: A freight forwarder's assistant extracts shipment fields from documents with inconsistent layouts and multilingual notes.
useCase.problem: The primary prompt occasionally mixes explanatory prose into a strict structured result or confuses optional fields with required ones.
useCase.requirement: The assistant must recover formatting and scope errors without guessing missing shipment identifiers.
useCase.architecture: A failure classifier selects a field-by-field extraction prompt only for known schema or coverage defects, using the same source passages.
runtime: The primary output fails a required-field schema check; the fallback asks for each field with a supporting span or explicit unknown.
The shared validator accepts the corrected structure only when values remain supported by the document.
useCase.failure: If the shipment identifier is absent, the fallback returns unknown and requests clarification instead of manufacturing a plausible number.
useCase.impact: Track fallback recovery by defect class, unsupported values, additional tokens, and document-type coverage. Prompt changes are justified by measured recovery rather than stylistic preference.

tradeoffs.benefit: Specific formatting or focus defects can recover.
tradeoffs.cost: Additional calls increase latency and spend.

tradeoffs.benefit: Alternate strategies preserve the same correctness contract.
tradeoffs.cost: Some useful partial outputs still require explicit separate contracts.
Too many branches become difficult to evaluate and maintain.

failures.scenario: Fallback drops a mandatory citation requirement
failures.detection: Invariant checks find missing evidence support.
failures.recovery: Reject the output and repair the template before reuse.

failures.scenario: A service outage triggers repeated prompt changes
failures.detection: Error classification identifies transport failure rather than content failure.
failures.recovery: Use timeout and failover policy instead.

mistakes.mistake: Using fallback to bypass policy refusals
mistakes.fix: Preserve policy and distinguish legitimate clarification from evasion.

mistakes.mistake: Trying many prompts without a budget
mistakes.fix: Limit strategy attempts and reserve finalization capacity.

mistakes.mistake: Treating missing facts as a wording problem

whenToUse: A known prompt-level defect has a tested alternate strategy.
All strategies can share clear acceptance criteria.
Recovery benefit exceeds the added latency and cost.
whenNotToUse: The failure is missing authority or unavailable evidence.
No evaluation demonstrates improved accepted outcomes.
checklist: Preserve invariant policy and evidence rules.
Measure recovery and regression by defect class.
